status_note: Draft self-inventory for Christian to confirm or edit before later interview-system phases build on it.

strengths.name: Dual-sided implementation translator
strengths.one_line: Translates between business and technical teams because he has implemented enterprise systems from both the vendor side and the internal owner side.
strengths.interview_safe: I translate between business and technical teams. I have implemented enterprise systems from both the vendor side and as the internal owner, so I can sit with a customer, understand what they actually need, turn it into something engineering can build, and make sure what is delivered still matches what was agreed.
strengths.how_it_shows_up: Discovery, requirements definition, FRD/SOW alignment, gap analysis, implementation judgment, and translating unclear needs into buildable scope.

strengths.name: Fast ramp on unfamiliar systems
strengths.one_line: Gets productive quickly in unfamiliar systems by mapping new tools to fundamentals he already understands.
strengths.interview_safe: I ramp quickly on unfamiliar systems. I have been handed platforms I had never used and gotten up to speed fast enough to train other teams on them, because I map new tools to fundamentals I already know. I am comfortable in ambiguity and I get productive fast.
strengths.how_it_shows_up: Learning velocity, self-direction, practical systems thinking, and becoming useful before every detail is known.

strengths.name: Cross-functional alignment without authority
strengths.one_line: Gets business, IT, finance, vendors, and leaders onto one usable plan even when ownership is split.
strengths.interview_safe: I am strong at aligning cross-functional groups without formal authority, getting business, IT, finance, and vendors onto one plan everyone commits to. I did exactly that on a five-month payment-integration project spanning four different organizations.
strengths.how_it_shows_up: Stakeholder alignment, influence without authority, executive communication, written confirmation, and delivery ownership across divided groups.

weaknesses.honest_name: rambles, buries the point, not BLUF
weaknesses.interview_safe: I tend to go deep into detail when I care about the work, so I have been deliberately practicing leading with the headline first and keeping answers tight, especially with non-technical and executive audiences.
weaknesses.improvement_action: Daily BLUF and story drills: answer first, one example, result, relevance, then stop.
weaknesses.improvement_spoken: so I have been drilling answer-first delivery: the headline, one example, the result, then I stop

weaknesses.honest_name: loses track of strengths, hedges, undersells
weaknesses.interview_safe: Historically I have undersold my own contributions by crediting the team and downplaying my part.
weaknesses.improvement_action: Maintain this self-inventory and a running evidence record so I can own my impact accurately without overstating it.
weaknesses.improvement_spoken: so I now keep a running record of my outcomes to own my impact accurately without overstating it

weaknesses.honest_name: no formal Lean Six Sigma belt, thinner on deep AI engineering, TOGAF, cloud and coding foundations
weaknesses.interview_safe: In a couple of areas my experience is hands-on rather than formally certified, for example I have led process-improvement work but have not sat for a Six Sigma belt.
weaknesses.improvement_action: Actively pursue the IT learning path so credentials and technical fluency catch up to the hands-on experience.
weaknesses.improvement_spoken: so I am actively working the certifications to catch the credentials up to the hands-on experience

signature_stories.name: Windows-95 discovery
signature_stories.summary: Aptean discovery uncovered hidden integration and infrastructure risk before ERP modernization work reached production.
signature_stories.spoken_reference: for example, at a client still running Windows-95-era systems, I led the discovery that surfaced the integration risks before they hit production
signature_stories.result: The project risk was surfaced during discovery instead of being discovered in production.

signature_stories.name: CEO escalation
signature_stories.summary: Took ownership of an executive escalation, reset alignment through written confirmation, and rebuilt customer trust.
signature_stories.spoken_reference: for example, when a client's CEO felt the delivered product did not match what was agreed, I took direct ownership, set a weekly cadence with him, fast-tracked the fixes with product and dev, and moved every agreement into writing
signature_stories.result: The relationship recovered and the account held.

signature_stories.name: East West fast ramp
signature_stories.summary: Ramped on an unfamiliar Aptean environment quickly enough to train global teams and own the system internally.
signature_stories.spoken_reference: for example, I was dropped into a platform I had never used at East West and got up to speed fast enough to train the global teams on it
signature_stories.result: I became productive quickly enough to train global teams and own the system internally.

signature_stories.name: EFT/ACH cross-functional replacement
signature_stories.summary: Coordinated IT, finance, Aptean, and Truist Bank through a five-month replacement of a fragile payment workflow.
signature_stories.spoken_reference: for example, a five-month EFT/ACH payment replacement where I aligned internal IT, global finance, the vendor, and the bank on one plan
signature_stories.result: The five-month replacement produced a compliant, auditable payment workflow across four parties.

signature_stories.name: Inventory automation / DMAIC
signature_stories.summary: Mapped and automated an inventory workflow, reducing manual work by 78%, discrepancies by 22%, and scrap cost by about 32%.
signature_stories.spoken_reference: for example, I mapped a messy inventory workflow, automated the control points, and reduced manual work by 78% while lowering discrepancies by 22%
signature_stories.result: The work reduced manual processing by 78%, lowered discrepancies by 22%, and cut scrap cost by about 32%.

motivation: What drives me is stepping into ambiguous, cross-functional problems, the ones without a clear owner, and turning them into structured work that people actually use and that holds up after I hand it off. I do my best work where business, operations, and technology have to line up, whatever the title, and I care most about closing the gap between a plan and something that actually works in practice.
non_negotiables: Do not invent credentials, metrics, ownership, or experience.
Lead with the point before adding context.
Use real stories and evidence rather than generic confidence language.
